title: fix(service-messaging)!: the in-app message door counts only accepted deliveries and refuses a send that reached nobody
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DXuamRUC67fx2TTYrFfyuSH)_

Fixes #32825

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — `POST /api/v1/messaging/in-app-messages` answered `200` when `emit()` accepted no delivery at all; it now answers `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` or `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` there. A picked recipient id longer than 255 characters, which no member can carry, is refused `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` where it was read. No export, route or body key is added.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: follow-up owed — content/docs/permissions/administrator-guide.mdx (its "Send an in-app message" passage says the confirmation counts the people the message went to, which is still true. It does not yet say that a send nobody received is refused, `503` or `409`, instead of confirmed. `skills/**` does not teach this door. The file is outside this card's lease, so the change is not in this PR.)

## Maintainer quick read

- What changes: the in-app message door now counts in `recipients` only the people a delivery was accepted for. When nobody was reached it no longer answers `200` "sent"; it answers `503` or `409`. One recipient id is bounded at 255 characters.
- Why: when the member read failed, no inbox channel was registered, or every delivery failed, the door still answered `200` with zero recipients and the console said "Message sent". An administrator would believe the message went out.
- Risk and rollback: this narrows a shipped door (shipped in 18.4.0). A call that answered `200` while reaching nobody now gets an error. The success shape is unchanged. Rollback is a revert of this PR; no data migration.
- Read first: `answerNobodyReached` in `packages/services/service-messaging/src/in-app-message-routes.ts` (where 503 or 409 is chosen), the new per-id length check in `parseInAppMessageBody` in the same file, and `.changeset/32825-in-app-message-honest-count.md`.
- Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-messaging exec vitest run src/in-app-message-routes.integration.test.ts`. Expect all 43 tests green, including the five new "the answer counts only accepted deliveries" cases.
- Needed from you: nothing; the seat lands it (as a narrowing it gets a contract-review-tier check before the queue).

## What changes

**N1: the answer counts only what was accepted, and a send that reached nobody is never a success.** `recipients` used to count every recipient a delivery was attempted for, so a failed delivery was counted too. It now counts a person only when at least one of their deliveries was accepted (delivered inline, or handed to the outbox). When `emit()` returns with no accepted delivery, the door refuses instead of answering `200` / `recipients: 0`, which the Setup action showed as "Message sent. Recipients: 0". The notification event row stays written as the record of the attempt. Which refusal is answered depends on what `EmitResult` shows:

| `emit()` reported | Answer |
|---|---|
| deliveries attempted, every one failed (no inbox channel registered, outbox write failed) | `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` through `sendServerFault`: the delivery errors go to the fault log, never onto the wire |
| inbox channel answered unavailable for the organization (`suppressed`) | `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` naming `channel: reason` |
| nothing attempted, `everyone: true` | `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. The resolver turns a failed `org:members` read into zero recipients, and the result cannot tell that apart from every member having turned `org.announcement` off. A failure has to be reported, so the door answers 503 and its message names both causes |
| nothing attempted, picked recipients | `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`: membership was read a step earlier and a `user:` selector resolves to itself, so every picked recipient turned the topic off |

Every code is an existing standard code (`StandardErrorCode`). No new code is added to the ADR-0112 ledger.

**Console (measured, no change needed).** The Setup action `send_in_app_message` (`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-notification.object.ts`) reads only `result.recipients` in its `successMessage`. The field keeps its name and shape. On a non-2xx answer the console's `api` handler (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx`, `if (!res.ok) … return refused(res, body)`) reports a failure carrying the envelope's message, so the dialog shows the refusal and no longer shows "Message sent".

**N2: one recipient id is bounded.** `IN_APP_MESSAGE_RECIPIENT_ID_MAX = 255`, the width of `sys_member.user_id` as the SQL driver stores a lookup. An id past it is refused `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` by its position (`'recipients' item N is L characters long …`) before any read, and the id itself is not repeated in the refusal. An id at the bound is still read and refused as a non-member like any other.

**N3: no send rate, by decision.** No rate limit is added. The route's docblock now has a "No send rate, by decision" section. The ruling that opened the door asked for no rate limit. Each request is already bounded by the request-body limit, at most `IN_APP_MESSAGE_RECIPIENTS_MAX` (1000) picked ids, the title, body, link and per-id bounds, and a sender who must hold `setup.write` in the organization they message. How often an administrator may message their own organization is a product decision for a later ruling.

**N4: an API-key test on this door.** A new `describe` in the door's shared harness file drives the door with `x-api-key` through the real `resolveMessagingCaller` composition, the way the plugin mounts it. It asserts what the preference-options door's credential-census test asserts: the auth service's trust rule receives the transport peer (`10.0.0.5`) and the raw `x-forwarded-for`, and the key's use stamp runs with the address that rule established (`203.0.113.7`) plus the user agent. The key's owner holds no `setup.write`, so the door then refuses `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` and nothing is sent.

## Tests

All new tests are in `packages/services/service-messaging/src/in-app-message-routes.integration.test.ts` (the door's existing harness file, top-level `describe`s): 9 new test cases. The harness gained two options, `inbox` (wrap or drop the real inbox channel) and `memberReadFails`.

- the answer counts only accepted deliveries (5): a failed delivery is counted in `failed`, not in `recipients` (`200`, `recipients: 1, delivered: 1, failed: 1`); no inbox channel ⇒ `503`, delivery errors not on the wire; inbox unavailable ⇒ `503` naming `inbox: transport_not_configured`; `everyone` with a failing `sys_member` read ⇒ `503`; every picked member opted out ⇒ `409`. Each asserts the envelope's `code` and `status` (ADR-0112) and that the inbox holds no row.
- one recipient id is bounded (2, plus one row in the closed-set refusal table): past the bound ⇒ `400` by position, id not echoed, no membership read, no emit; at the bound ⇒ read, refused as a non-member.
- an API key hands its client facts to the key's use stamp (1).

## Acceptance notes

- The `everyone` / nobody-reached case answers `503` even when the real cause is that every member opted out. `EmitResult` does not separate "zero recipients resolved" from "every recipient filtered by preference", and adding that to `emit()`'s result would change the messaging service's contract, which is outside this card. The refusal message names both causes. If a later card wants `409` for the opted-out case, the change belongs in `EmitResult`, not in this door.
- `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` 503s are logged once per route per process as a declared capability absence (`logServerFault`'s quieting). The failed-delivery arm sends the delivery errors as the logged `thrown`.

## Verification

<details><summary>Local runs: commands, exit codes, counts</summary>

All runs are on head `72a6c3a8` (merge base `e540baf8`), in worktree `objectstack-a2-32825`.

- Dependency closure: `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/service-messaging^...' build`. Lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- The door's two files: `vitest run src/in-app-message-routes.integration.test.ts src/in-app-message-action.test.ts`. `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 47 passed (47)`.
- Package: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-messaging test`. `Test Files 71 passed (71)`, `Tests 958 passed (958)`, exit 0.
- Package typecheck: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-messaging typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` over `src`, test files included, plus `tsconfig.scripts.json`). Exit 0.
- Ablation N1, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. The anchor `const reached = new Set(result.deliveries.filter((d) => d.ok)…).size;` was replaced with a count of every delivery `|| 1`. The anchor went from 1 occurrence to 0 and the blob changed from `6a05b005a743` to `2045cb71f4fa`. 5 tests failed, 38 passed (43): exactly the five "answer counts only accepted deliveries" cases. Afterwards the blob was restored to equal HEAD and `git diff HEAD` was empty.
- Ablation N2, same tool. `if (overlong >= 0) {` was replaced with `if (overlong >= 0 && false) {`. 2 tests failed, 41 passed: the refusal-table row and the "never echoing it" case. Restored to the HEAD blob.
- The test file imports the route by relative source path, so the ablation needs no `dist/` rebuild.
- Derived gates: `dispatch-gates --commands` derived 65 families. `--ran` with recorded exit codes: `65 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 61 run, 4 NOT-MEASURED (4 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)`. All 61 that ran exited 0. These 4 are NOT MEASURED, each because a prerequisite was missing (exit 3): `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` (the shallow clone cannot reach its pinned fixture commit), `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (it needs every package's `dist/`), `check:i18n` (it needs the built CLI closure, and this diff touches no translation source), and `check:type-check-debt` (its own lock queue timed out). CI runs all four.
- `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs`: OK.
- Full dogfood battery: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test`, on this head, after `--filter '@objectstack/dogfood^...' build`. Lock `VERDICT command-exit 1`. Result: `Test Files 5 failed | 459 passed | 3 skipped (467)`, `Tests 6 failed | 3921 passed | 42 skipped (3969)`. All 6 failures are `Test timed out in 5000ms`, in five files that do not exercise messaging: `bare-name-one-holder-ai-family`, `external-import-walled-catalog-refusal`, `flow-provenance-server-held` (2 tests), `package-commit-revert-path-package` and `security-verdict-follows-runtime-metadata-change`. The battery held the lock for 1h01m on a shared box. Rerunning those five files on the same head gave `Test Files 5 passed (5)`, `Tests 68 passed (68)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. No dogfood test drives `/api/v1/messaging/in-app-messages`.

</details>
